title: a-commit-reseals-only-the-seals-whose-closure-it-changes
intention: A commit reseals only the seals whose recorded closure contains a file the commit changes — the changed proof itself, plus the owning component's proofs whose fingerprint_closure names a staged file — so adding one proof reseals one seal, never the whole component serially.
why: RULE 1 in Akien's words: "we'd only have to run the tests for the changed files and not for all files." On 2026-10-05 a commit adding one proof to cairn/devices/tester ran past a 30-minute limit inside the pre-commit reseal: proofs_touching selects all 33 of the owning component's proofs and reseals them serially; one, test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument.py, took 793s alone (a measurement, its own smell). The lived symptom is a builder's one-file commit that cannot land in half an hour, re-deriving verdicts whose closures never moved (Law 1).
traces_to: RULE 1 (Akien, 2026-10-01: 'we'd only have to run the tests for the changed files and not for all files'); Law 1 (re-running a proof whose closure did not move re-derives a settled verdict); foreground-decisions item 7 ('tool proofs: agreed' — the reseal door re-runs only the changed component's proofs, 'via fingerprint_closure')
how: In cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py proofs_touching(): keep the owner filter (Akien's 'tool proofs: agreed', foreground-decisions item 7) and narrow within it — a proof of an owning component is selected when it is itself staged, or its standing seal's fingerprint_closure (closure_of) contains a staged path, or it has no seal, or its seal predates closures (closure_of is None: the whole-component recipe answers, conservative). Everything else in the owning component is left alone; component_color still reds any seal whose fingerprint moved. Proof under cairn/devices/tester/proofs/, written red. The census of closures follows the CENSUS SPLIT recorded in the falsifier. Clause 2 (KILLED MID-RUN, in the falsifier): stage each seal in the act of writing it, or adopt a reproducing leftover at the next run's start — the builder picks whichever is smaller in reseal.py, and the tooth judges both.
falsifier: GREEN when a proof under cairn/devices/tester/proofs/ builds a fixture component with three sealed proofs whose closures are disjoint, stages one NEW proof file, and proofs_touching returns exactly that one proof; staging a file named in one sealed proof's closure returns exactly that proof plus none of the others; a proof with no seal and a pre-closure seal are each selected. WRONG INTENT if the recorded closures are too coarse to separate proofs (every tester seal naming every tester file), which a census of the 33 tester seals' fingerprint_closure measures first. Measured beside it: the 793s proof is test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument.py. CENSUS SPLIT (the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0, 2026-10-05): 184d211153ff narrowed a seal's closure to its own component's files (validation_store.repo_relative_closure + _owned_by_the_proofs_component, build f5376a4a 15:10:18, PROVED ae004432 15:11:52 -0600). The n=1 measurement above — test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument's 45-file multi-component closure — was sealed at 15:05:44, BEFORE that build, so it is an old wide closure and says nothing about separation. The census splits every tester seal by sealed-before vs after ae004432 and judges 'can closures separate proofs' ONLY on post-184d closures, or on what repo_relative_closure returns for each proof now (computable without resealing). A pre-184d wide closure counted as evidence would fire WRONG INTENT falsely. KILLED MID-RUN (clause 2, the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0, 2026-10-05; measured on b312: the 17:06 pre-commit was killed after writing 16 green seals it never staged, and the PROVED clearance's working_tree_clean lane refused until they were committed by hand at e8182202): GREEN also when a reseal killed mid-run leaves no unstaged seal that blocks the next clearance — either reseal stages each seal as it writes it, or the next run adopts a leftover unstaged seal whose fingerprint reproduces at HEAD (sealed_fingerprint_now == evidence.source_fingerprint) and leaves a non-reproducing one red. Tooth: a fixture reseal interrupted after writing one seal, followed by the next run, leaves the working tree clean of that seal with it staged or committed; a leftover whose fingerprint does not reproduce is not adopted. The tester owns what a run it started leaves behind (foreground-decisions 8d/8e), whatever killed it: timeout, lost session, OOM.
watchme: none, because the consumer is the next commit that touches cairn/devices/tester: the pre-commit hook cairn/devices/tester/hooks/pre-commit prints which proofs it resealed, and that count is the measurement this ticket bounds
children: none, because the change is one selection function in one device with one proof
